article.title: Present Perfect vs. Past Simple
article.description: Present Perfect (have/has + past participle) is used for actions with a connection to now, or when the exact time isn't stated: 'I have visited Paris.' Past Simple is used for finished actions at a specific, stated past time: 'I visited Paris in 2019.' Common mistake: using Present Perfect with a specific past time marker, e.g. 'I have visited Paris in 2019' is incorrect — should be Past Simple.
article.content: Present Perfect (have/has + past participle) is used for actions with a connection to now, or when the exact time isn't stated: 'I have visited Paris.' Past Simple is used for finished actions at a specific, stated past time: 'I visited Paris in 2019.' Common mistake: using Present Perfect with a specific past time marker, e.g. 'I have visited Paris in 2019' is incorrect — should be Past Simple.

generated.caption:
Ever said "I have visited Paris in 2019" and felt unsure? 🤔 Here's a quick fix!

Use Present Perfect for actions connected to now or when the exact time isn't stated.
Use Past Simple for finished actions at a specific past time.
So, say 'I visited Paris in 2019,' not 'I have visited Paris in 2019.' Easy!

generated.script: Kabhi socha hai 'I have visited Paris in 2019' galat kyu hai? Dekho, Present Perfect (have/has + past participle) hum tab use karte hain jab action ka connection present se ho, ya exact time bataya na gaya ho. Jaise, 'I have visited Paris.' Yahan koi specific time nahi hai. Lekin, Past Simple use hota hai jab action ho gaya hai aur uska exact time mention kiya gaya ho. Jaise, 'I visited Paris in 2019.' Isliye, 'I have visited Paris in 2019' bolna galat hai kyuki yahan time '2019' clearly diya hai. Toh yaad rakho, jab bhi sentence mein exact time mention ho — jaise 'yesterday', 'last year', ya 'in 2019' — always use Past Simple. Simple! Comment karke batao ye tip aapko pata thi ya nahi! slides.body: The Present Perfect (have/has + past participle) describes actions connected to the present, or when the exact time isn't specified, like 'I have visited Paris.' In contrast, the Past Simple describes finished actions at a specific, stated past time: 'I visited Paris in 2019.' A common mistake is using the Present Perfect with a specific past time marker; for example, 'I have visited Paris in 2019' is incorrect. Remember, 'I visited Paris in 2019' is the correct usage for a definite past event.
